description: An eight-slot sampler played from a keyboard, with a key zone and its own settings for each slot, routed to eight stereo outputs

params.text: Sets the level of the recording inputs, 0 to 200%
Starts and stops recording into the slot the SLOT knob has selected
Passes the recording inputs through to the outputs
Chooses which of the eight slots every control below it acts on, 1 to 8
Sets the MIDI note number, 0 to 127, for whichever part of the selected slot's key zone the KEY SELECT button has picked
Steps through which part of the selected slot's key zone the KEY knob sets: lowest note, highest note, reference note. Holding it about a second starts MIDI learn
Chooses which of the eight stereo outputs the selected slot is sent to, 1 to 8; more than one slot can share an output
Sets where the selected slot's playback begins and its attack starts, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where the selected slot's playback ends and its release starts, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where the selected slot's loop begins, as a percentage of the sample
Sets where the selected slot's loop ends, as a percentage of the sample
Plays the selected slot backwards, from its cue end towards its cue start
Sets the selected slot's crossfade at a loop join, the fade before the end of the sample, and the fade in and out of a recording, 1ms to 10 seconds
Plays the selected slot between its loop cursors over and over instead of stopping at the cue end
Reverses the selected slot's playback direction at the cursors instead of jumping back, so the sample runs forwards and backwards in turn
Chooses whether the selected slot is played for as long as the gate is held or started by a trigger
Chooses what a trigger does on the selected slot: Start/Stop alternates, Restart plays from the cue start every time
Lets the selected slot follow the PB input; with it off that slot keeps its pitch while others bend
Moves the selected slot's cue and loop cursors to the nearest zero crossings, which stops loop clicks; it should be off for one-cycle waveforms
Sets how long the selected slot's envelope takes to rise, 1ms to 10 seconds
Sets how long the selected slot's envelope takes to fall to its sustain level, 1ms to 10 seconds
Sets the level the selected slot's envelope holds at, 0% to 100%
Sets how long the selected slot's envelope takes to fall to silence, 1ms to 10 seconds
Bends the selected slot's envelope curve between exponential, linear and logarithmic
Lengthens or shortens the selected slot without changing its pitch, 1% to 999%, with 100% leaving it alone
Sets the length of the repeated cycle the selected slot's time-stretch is built from, 1ms to 99ms
Sets the selected slot's own level, 0% to 100%
Loads the previous file in the same folder into the selected slot
Loads the next file in the same folder into the selected slot

inputs.text: The left channel to be recorded; recording is only possible with a cable in here
The right channel to be recorded, which makes the recording stereo
Plays whichever slots the incoming note falls inside: held high in gate mode, or a trigger in trigger mode; its channel count sets the polyphony
The note to play, one octave per volt, matched against each slot's key zone and pitched from that slot's reference note
Sets the level of each note played, per channel of polyphony
Bends the pitch of the slots whose PB button is on, over the range chosen under Pitch Bend Range

outputs.text: The left channel of whichever slots are routed to that output
The right channel of whichever slots are routed to that output

notes: nothing plays until a sample is loaded or recorded into a slot: choose the slot with the SLOT knob, then right-click the panel and use Load Sample, or right-click the waveform display.
nothing plays either until the selected slot has a key zone that the incoming note falls inside; a zone may be a single note, for percussion.
every control below the SLOT knob acts on the one slot that knob has selected, so the panel shows one slot's settings at a time.
recording needs a cable in the left recording input; with that jack empty the REC button does nothing.
a key zone is three notes: the lowest and highest it answers to, and the reference note that is the sample's own recorded pitch.
menu: Load Sample — opens a file chooser for the selected slot
Save FULL Sample — writes the selected slot's whole sample to a wav file
Save CUE Region — writes the part between the selected slot's cue cursors to a wav file
Save LOOP Region — writes the part between the selected slot's loop cursors to a wav file
Trim Sample after Save — keeps only the saved part in memory afterwards, instead of keeping the whole sample
Save Oversampled — writes the file at the module's internal rate, twice Rack's, for editing elsewhere
Select Samples Root — picks a folder, after which a Samples Browser submenu appears for loading
Quantize incoming v/Oct — rounds the V/Oct input to the nearest semitone, which stops an imprecise voltage giving a pitch between notes
Pitch Bend Range: 1 semitone to 11 semitones, 1 octave, 2 octaves, 3 octaves, 4 octaves — sets how far the PB input bends the pitch
Anti-aliasing filter — adds two-times oversampling and a 20kHz lowpass before the outputs
Polyphonic OUTs — carries the polyphony of the played notes through to the outputs; with it off the voices are summed into single-channel outputs
Polyphonic Master IN — lets the velocity jack take a polyphonic cable matching the gate channels
Auto Monitor Off — turns monitoring off by itself once a recording stops
Disable NAV Buttons — stops the panel navigation buttons from loading anything, so they cannot be pressed by accident
Reset cursors on Load — puts the selected slot's cue and loop cursors back to 0% and 100% whenever a new sample is loaded
Presets: Wavetable, Triggered Sample with Envelope, Drum Player — sets the selected slot's cursors, mode and envelope in one go for one of three common uses
Store Sample in Patch — saves the loaded samples inside the patch file, which can make it very large
Unlimited REC (risky) — lifts the memory ceiling on recording, at the risk of a crash on a recording the machine cannot hold
